unclear: REPO holds three separate task implementations and no single top-level model: hotpotqa_runs/agents.py (CoTAgent, ReactAgent, ReactReflectAgent), alfworld_runs (run_trial + update_memory) and programming_runs/reflexion.py (run_reflexion). The graph follows ReactReflectAgent because it has every draft part (environment, Actor, Evaluator, Self-Reflection, both memories); edges that only exist in another implementation say so in the label.

The draft's 'memory' container has no code counterpart: short-term memory is the scratchpad string and long-term memory is the reflections list, two unrelated attributes; so no 'memory' component is emitted and both have parent null.
Draft env -> actor (o_t): in code observations are appended to the scratchpad (short-term memory) and reach the Actor only through it; drawn as env -> short_term_mem -> actor.

Draft evaluator -> self_reflection (r_t): in HotPotQA the reward reaches the reflection LLM only as the text 'Answer is CORRECT/INCORRECT' inside the scratchpad, and as the gate that decides whether reflect() runs at all. In programming the reflection gets the textual unit-test report (feedback), in ALFWorld no reward text at all (reflection is only run when the trial failed).
Draft long_term_mem -> self_reflection (mem): only ALFWorld passes past reflections into the reflection prompt; HotPotQA's _build_reflection_prompt and the programming self_reflection do not.

Draft Ω bound (1-3): ALFWorld uses the last 3 entries; HotPotQA under REFLEXION keeps all reflections (unbounded) and under LAST_ATTEMPT_AND_REFLEXION keeps only the newest one; programming passes only the latest reflection to func_impl (the reflections list is kept for logging).

In the programming implementation the Actor (func_impl with strategy='reflexion') also receives the previous implementation and the test feedback directly, not only the reflection; the Evaluator inside the loop runs self-generated tests, and the hidden benchmark tests (exe.evaluate with item['test']) are only used to score the final answer.

The HotPotQA trial loop (calling agent.run() repeatedly) and the ALFWorld outer loop over trials are not in REPO; the evaluator -> actor control edge cites ALFWorld's skip of already-solved environments. programming_runs/reflexion.py does contain its loop (while cur_iter < max_iters, break when tests pass).
Evaluator is a fixed function (exact match / env success flag / unit-test executor) in all three implementations; no LLM-as-evaluator appears in REPO.
Actor and Self-Reflection are separate LLM instances in HotPotQA (same gpt-3.5-turbo by default); in programming the same `model` object serves both. No model parameters are ever updated.
Shapes/resolutions do not apply: all tensors are strings (prompts, scratchpads, reflections).
